title: ESM-FEP combines protein-language-model fitness screening and free-energy calculations to engineer herbicide-detoxifying maize dioxygenase
summary: ESM-FEP was applied to Zea mays dioxygenase ZmHSL1B and nominated a quadruple mutant (Q140H/Y205F/L332R/K336F) with approximately sevenfold higher catalytic efficiency for mesotrione detoxification than wild type, measured by in-vitro assays and kinetic analysis. Arabidopsis thaliana expressing the engineered variant showed enhanced herbicide tolerance in the reported transgenic tests.
ai_technology: ESM-FEP (fine-tuned ESM-2 protein language model plus alchemical free-energy perturbation)
organization: Central China Normal University, State Key Laboratory of Green Pesticide

evidence.tested: ESM-FEP was applied to Zea mays dioxygenase ZmHSL1B and nominated a quadruple mutant (Q140H/Y205F/L332R/K336F) with approximately sevenfold higher catalytic efficiency for mesotrione detoxification than wild type, measured by in-vitro assays and kinetic analysis.
evidence.unknown: Reported results concern one maize dioxygenase and mesotrione in specified in-vitro and Arabidopsis tests. They do not establish crop-field performance, commercial efficacy, or generality across herbicides/enzymes. Primary PubMed abstract and publisher citation metadata checked; no independent replication assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Fine-tuned ESM-2 screened saturation-mutagenesis variants for retained global protein fitness; free-energy perturbation then estimated substrate-binding effects and prioritized mutants. The selected M5 mutant was assayed in vitro and in transgenic Arabidopsis by the researchers.
